message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “no seat‑belt” law applies to all vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield to the right” rule applies at uncontrolled intersections. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• “No passing” zones on two‑lane roads. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and permit zones apply in cities. | Local city ordinances | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or abandoned.
• Towing a vehicle without proper authorization can lead to fines. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Roadside Assistance & Accident Reporting** | • Report accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 to the police. | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT** – Official website for state‑wide traffic regulations and updates. - **TxDMV** – For registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. - **Texas Department of Public Safety** – For DUI laws, accident reporting, and enforcement. - **Local City Ordinances** – Check your city’s website for specific parking, speed, and local traffic rules. --- #### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they are the law. 2. **Use hands‑free** – keep your phone out of your hands while driving. 3. **Check your vehicle’s inspection status** – a failed inspection can lead to a ticket. 4. **Know your local rules** – city ordinances can differ from state law (e.g., parking restrictions). Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
